texts.li: [theirLowtech] Among {FACTION}, a war leader called {X_nameFull} has gathered the hardest of their fighters into one band, {NAME}, and burned two villages before the elders could agree what to do about {X_objective}.\n\nThe band rides out of {PLACE} and comes home with grain and cattle, and every raid brings it more riders. {X_nameDef} has let it be known that the colony is on the list.

[theirHightech,!lowtech] The traders' radio has carried one name all week: {X_nameFull}. A raider of {FACTION} who started with one truck and a handful of guns, {X_nameDef} now leads {NAME}, the largest band anyone in the region remembers, out of {PLACE}.\n\nTwo outposts have gone quiet this season. The last message from one of them mentioned the colony by name, as the next place worth a visit.

{FACTION} have a new war leader. {X_nameFull} beat every rival for the place in open fight, and the band that follows {X_objective} now calls itself {NAME}.\n\nFrom {PLACE} they strike at anything within a few days' ride. The colony is within a few days' ride, and {X_nameDef} knows it.

[winter] Winter hasn't slowed {FACTION}. A war leader among them, {X_nameFull}, has taken their hungriest fighters and made them into a band called {NAME}. They raid wherever the snow lets them through, and take what they need to last the cold.\n\nThe colony has food in its stores. {X_nameDef} will know that by now.

[summer] With the roads dry and the nights short, {FACTION} have found a leader worth following. {X_nameFull} has pulled their raiding parties together into one band, {NAME}, and spent the summer so far stripping the farms around {PLACE} bare.\n\nThe colony is next on the road, and {X_nameDef} has not passed a farm by yet.

summaries.li: [!truce,!captured] Raids from {FACTION} come more often and hit harder, and {X_nameDef} leads some of them. It ends when {X_nameDef} falls (at the colony's walls, to the neighbors, or to a bounty hunter) or when {NAME} breaks up for want of plunder.
[truce] {X_nameDef} has been paid to leave the colony alone, and {NAME} is raiding elsewhere for now. Raids from {FACTION} are back to what they were.
[captured] {X_nameDef} is the colony's prisoner, and {NAME} has nobody to lead it.

texts.li: [!hunters,!broken] A rider came to the gate under a white cloth and gave {X_nameDef}'s words exactly as they were given: "{COUNT} silver, and {NAME} rides past. Refuse, and we come in."\n\nThe council has argued since. Paying would buy quiet, for a while. A price on {X_nameDef}'s head, posted in every town that will take it, would set hunters on {X_objective}. Or the colony can hold its walls and let the band find out how little there is to take.

[hunters,!ally,!broken] {X_nameDef} has named a price: {COUNT} silver, and {NAME} will ride past the colony. The rider who brought the message left before anyone could answer.\n\n{ENEMY} are hunting {X_nameDef} already, and are short of everything a long hunt needs. A purse of silver would go a long way with them. A bounty would bring hunters of every other kind. Or the colony can sit tight and let the band starve of plunder.

[hunters,ally,!broken] {X_nameDef} has sent word: {COUNT} silver, and {NAME} will look elsewhere for plunder.\n\nThere are other answers. {ENEMY}, the colony's allies, have been fighting {FACTION} for years; asked, they would march on {NAME} in force, though it would cost them fighters and they would want that remembered. Silver for their riders, or a price on {X_nameDef}'s head, would cost the colony less. Or the council can wait the band out.

[hunters,broken] {X_nameDef} took the colony's silver once and came back anyway. Now another rider is at the gate, talking about a price.\n\nThe council won't hear of paying twice. {ENEMY} are still hunting {X_objective}, and a bounty would bring others. The band may yet break up on its own.

[!hunters,broken] Another rider from {X_nameDef}, another price. The last silver the colony paid bought a few days' quiet, and then the band came back.\n\nThe council won't hear of paying twice. A bounty would bring hunters from every town that will post it. Or the colony can hold its walls and let the band wear itself out.

li.label: Pay {X_objective} off ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The rider counts the silver at the gate and rides off with it. {NAME} will go elsewhere, for as long as the bargain holds.
li.riskOutcome: The rider counts the silver at the gate and rides off with it. {NAME} will go elsewhere, for as long as the bargain holds.

li.label: Post a bounty ({ITEM} silver)
li.outcome: Notices go out with every trader and traveler: {ITEM} silver for {X_nameDef}, brought in alive or dead. The silver goes with them, sealed, to be held for whoever collects.

li.label: Send silver to {ENEMY} ({DAYS} silver)
li.outcome: A rider of {ENEMY} comes for the silver and is gone again before dark. Their hunters will be better fed and better armed for it.
li.deed: sent silver to {ENEMY} for the hunt

li.label: Ask {ENEMY} to march
li.outcome: {ENEMY} agree to march on {NAME}. It will cost them, and they make sure the colony knows it. Their army will be on the road within days.

li.label: Wait {X_objective} out
li.outcome: The council gives {X_nameDef} nothing: no silver and no answer. Let {NAME} find out how little there is to take here.

texts.li: The army of {ENEMY} met {NAME} in the hills beyond {PLACE}, and came off worse. They are back behind their walls counting their dead, and some of them lay that at the colony's door.\n\n{X_nameDef} is still out there, and prouder for it.

[enemyLowtech] {ENEMY} marched against {NAME} with banners flying and came home three days later with their wounded in carts. {X_nameDef} met them at a river crossing and held it.\n\nThe band will be bolder for this. {ENEMY} will not be asked again soon.

[hunters] {X_nameDef} is in the colony's cells, and {NAME} has nobody to lead it. Word travels fast: by morning, everyone between here and {PLACE} will know.\n\n{ENEMY} have sent a rider to ask for {X_objective}. They have a long list of grievances and mean to try {X_objective} for every one. {FACTION} have sent a rider too, with {COUNT} silver, to buy {X_objective} back.

[!hunters] The colony has {X_nameDef} in a cell, and {NAME} has nobody to lead it.\n\n{FACTION} have sent a rider with {COUNT} silver to buy {X_objective} back. The colony can take the silver, or keep {X_nameDef} and decide what to do about {X_objective} in its own time.

li.label: Keep {X_objective}
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} stays in the cells. Whatever happens to {X_objective} now is the colony's business.

li.label: Hand {X_objective} over to {ENEMY}
li.outcome: Riders of {ENEMY} come for {X_nameDef} at first light and take {X_objective} away in chains.

li.label: Take the ransom ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {FACTION}'s rider counts out {COUNT} silver at the gate, and {X_nameDef} walks out past it without a word to anyone.

texts.li: [revenge] {X_nameDef} is dead, brought down at the colony by {B_nameDef}, who had more reason than most. {NAME} scattered before nightfall.\n\nIn {PLACE} they will tell it as a story, and not one they enjoy telling.

[slayer] {B_nameDef} brought {X_nameDef} down at the colony's own walls. Without {X_objective}, {NAME} is a crowd of tired fighters a long way from home, and it is already breaking up.\n\nIn the towns around {PLACE}, they are drinking to the colony tonight.
[diedCaptive] {X_nameDef} died in the colony's hands. {NAME} did not outlive {X_objective} by long: the band broke up within days, each fighter making for home with whatever could be carried.

[!diedCaptive] {X_nameDef} is dead. {NAME} came to the colony for plunder and lost its leader instead, and its fighters are already drifting home.\n\nThe neighbors have heard. For a while, the colony's name will mean something on the roads.

{X_nameDef} stays in the colony's cells, and {NAME} is finished. The band's fighters have gone home in twos and threes, and none of {FACTION}'s captains is in a hurry to take up {X_possessive} banner.\n\nWhat becomes of {X_nameDef} is up to the colony now.

{NAME} waited three days outside {PLACE} for a leader who wasn't coming back. Then the fighters started to leave. {X_nameDef} sits in the colony's cells and hears the news from whoever brings the food.

Riders of {ENEMY} took {X_nameDef} to {PLACE} to answer for {NAME}'s raids. Whatever they decide, {X_nameDef} won't trouble the region again.\n\n{ENEMY} won't forget who handed {X_objective} over. Neither will {FACTION}.

[enemyLowtech] {X_nameDef} went to {PLACE} in a cart, in irons, with half of {ENEMY} lining the road to watch. The trial will be short.\n\nThe colony's part in it is the talk of every hall between here and there.

li.chronicle: The colony handed {X_nameDef} over to {ENEMY} for trial.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} rode home with {FACTION}'s silver paid, and the colony is richer by {COUNT}. {NAME} broke up anyway. Few fighters want to follow a leader who had to be bought out of a cell.\n\n{X_nameDef} is alive, and remembers the inside of that cell.

li.chronicle: The colony let {FACTION} ransom {X_nameDef} for {COUNT} silver.

texts.li: [takenAlive] Riders of {ENEMY} caught up with {X_nameDef} at the ford below {PLACE} and took {X_objective} alive. The rest of {NAME} scattered into the hills without a fight.\n\n{ENEMY} mean to put {X_nameDef} on trial. However that goes, the colony has seen the last of {X_objective}.

[!takenAlive] {X_nameDef} is dead, brought down by riders of {ENEMY} in a fight near {PLACE} that was over in an afternoon. {NAME} broke and ran as soon as its leader fell.\n\nThe news reached the colony with a trader two days later.

[gifts,!takenAlive,enemyLowtech] {ENEMY} cornered {X_nameDef} in the hills above {PLACE}, on horses and with bread the colony's silver paid for. {X_nameDef} did not come down again.\n\n{ENEMY} have sent a rider to tell the colony so, and to say thank you.

[gifts,!takenAlive,enemyHightech] {ENEMY} ran {X_nameDef} to ground near {PLACE}, in trucks and with ammunition the colony's silver paid for. {NAME} is finished.\n\n{ENEMY} have sent word to say so, and to say thank you.
[winter] The snow did half the work. {ENEMY} found {X_nameDef}'s camp by its smoke, in the hills near {PLACE}, and {NAME} had no fight left in it after a cold month of short rations.

[named,takenAlive,lowtech] {OTHER_nameDef}, a bounty hunter out of {PLACE}, brought {X_nameDef} in alive, tied across a saddle. The colony's notice was the reason, and the colony's silver paid for it.\n\n{NAME} has broken up. The roads are quieter already.

[named,takenAlive,!lowtech] {X_nameDef} came in alive, in the back of a truck driven by {OTHER_nameDef}, a bounty hunter out of {PLACE}. The colony's notice was the reason, and the colony's silver paid for it.\n\n{NAME} has broken up. The roads are quieter already.

[named,!takenAlive] {OTHER_nameDef}, a bounty hunter working out of {PLACE}, tracked {X_nameDef} for nine days and brought {X_objective} down on the tenth. The colony's silver has changed hands, and {NAME} has broken up for good.

[!named] A hunter the colony has never seen brought {X_nameDef} down and collected the bounty, with proof enough for the trader holding the silver.\n\n{NAME} has broken up. The roads are quieter already.

li.chronicle: A bounty hunter brought down {X_nameDef} of {NAME}.

texts.li: [takenAlive] The army of {ENEMY} met {NAME} on open ground near {PLACE} and broke it before noon. {X_nameDef} was taken alive and will stand trial.\n\n{ENEMY} marched because the colony asked. They lost good people doing it, and they expect that to be remembered.

[!takenAlive] The army of {ENEMY} caught {NAME} on open ground near {PLACE}. {X_nameDef} fell in the first charge, and the band ran.\n\n{ENEMY} marched because the colony asked. They lost good people doing it, and they expect that to be remembered.

li.chronicle: At the colony's asking, {ENEMY} broke {NAME} near {PLACE}.

texts.li: The company the colony hired, led by {OTHER_nameDef}, fell on {FACTION} at {PLACE}. {X_nameDef} was there, and did not come out of it.\n\nThe colony's silver bought more than anyone expected. {NAME} is finished.

li.chronicle: Mercenaries in the colony's pay brought down {X_nameDef} of {NAME}.

texts.li: [truce,theirLowtech] {X_nameDef} kept the bargain, more or less. {NAME} raided elsewhere all season, and now the band has broken up: fighters gone home, horses sold, {X_nameDef} gone with a few loyal riders and nobody sure where.\n\nThe colony paid for its quiet. At the council table, some still call that wise.

[truce,theirHightech] {X_nameDef} kept the bargain, more or less. {NAME} raided elsewhere all season, and now the band has broken up: fighters gone home, trucks sold for parts, {X_nameDef} gone with a few loyal followers and nobody sure where.\n\nThe colony paid for its quiet, and there are some at the council table who haven't stopped saying so.

[broken] After the broken truce, {NAME} never found its feet again. Its fighters wanted plunder and got hard knocks, and one by one they went home. {X_nameDef} rode out of the region with a handful of the loyal.\n\nThe colony's silver is gone, but so is the band.

[repelled,!truce,!broken] {NAME} has broken up. Every raid it sent at the colony came back with less than it cost to send, and that is the kind of story that ends a band.\n\n{X_nameDef} left the region with a handful of loyal riders, and without a coin of the colony's silver.

[!repelled,!truce,!broken] {NAME} has broken up. A season of raiding brought it less than it promised, and fighters who aren't paid in plunder go home. {X_nameDef} left the region with a handful of loyal riders.\n\nThe colony waited {X_objective} out.

li.chronicle: {NAME} broke up, and {X_nameDef} left the region.

texts.li: {FACTION} are finished, and {NAME} with them. With nothing to go home to, the band has scattered, and {X_nameDef} has not been seen since.
{FACTION} have made peace with the colony, and there is no place in that peace for {X_nameDef}. {NAME} has been told to disband, and has. {X_nameDef} left {PLACE} the same night.
{X_nameDef} hasn't been seen in days. Some say a fever in the hills, some say a knife in the back from one of {X_possessive} own. {NAME} has broken up either way, and the roads are quieter for it.

[!nohunters] {FACTION} have enemies of their own. {ENEMY} have been fighting them for years, and their riders are already out looking for {X_nameDef}. Every day the band stays in the field, the hunters get closer.

[!nohunters] {FACTION} have enemies of their own. {ENEMY} have scouts out on every road from {PLACE}, and they want {X_nameDef} more than anyone. The longer the band stays in the field, the likelier they are to catch it.

[nohunters] None of the region's peoples is at war with {FACTION} openly enough to go after {X_nameDef}. Bands like this one break up when the plunder runs dry, or when someone puts a price on the leader's head.
{NAME} attacks
[leads] {X_nameDef} rides
[leads] {X_nameDef} at the gate
[leads] {NAME} has come for the colony, and {X_nameDef} rides at the front. Bring {X_objective} down here and the band is finished.
[leads,theirLowtech] Horns on the road: {NAME} has come for the colony, with {X_nameDef}'s banner in the middle of it. Every fighter here knows what it would mean to bring {X_objective} down today.
[!leads] Riders of {NAME} have come to the colony. {X_nameDef} isn't with them this time, but they are {X_possessive} people, and they will tell {X_objective} how it went.
[!leads] A war party of {NAME} is moving on the colony. {X_nameDef} stayed behind at {PLACE} and sent the hungriest. How they do here decides how big the band is next month.
{X_nameDef} breaks the truce
The silver bought less time than the council hoped. {X_nameDef} has spent it, and {NAME} is back at the colony with {X_objective} at its head.\n\nThere won't be another offer.
[theirLowtech] {X_nameDef}'s word was worth exactly what the colony paid for it, and not a day more. {NAME} is on the road again, and the road leads here.
{X_nameDef}, the warlord of {NAME}, rides with them. Bring {X_objective} down here and the band is finished.
